WHAT SURPRISED ME — the biggest item first

1. SCOPE IS A TEST COUNT, NOT A TEST COST, AND READING THE TEST NAMES REVERSES THE RANKING. This is the main finding and it is not visible anywhere in the CSV. jekyll-8167 clears the gate at scope 20, but all 20 selected tests are `Utils.slugify` string-regex assertions on short strings — microseconds each — so its fence is minitest boot and nothing else (est. 3-10 core-s, near-certain layer-3 reject). I initially wrote fpm-1829 off the same way from its first 8 P2P ('should default to native', 'should convert x86_64 to amd64'), then read all 41 and reversed: roughly 18 of them are `#output` specs that build a real .deb and read fields back through a dpkg_field helper, including three compression-variant tests (gz/bz2/xz) and 'should output bit-for-bit identical packages', and the new F2P describe block builds and re-reads a package for each of 11 provides values. Same scope column, opposite cost. Recommendation: the layer-2 repo probe is not optional for Ruby, it is the only instrument that separates rubocop and fpm from jekyll, fluentd, fastlane and faker.

2. RUBY'S REPO DIVERSITY IS AN ARTEFACT OF COUNTING PRE-GATE, AND THIS EXPOSES A DEFECT IN STEP 2d. Ruby looks like the best-spread language in the corpus: 6 repos, max repo share 36% (rubocop 16/44), so W-CONFOUND correctly does not fire. But selection happens on the ELIGIBLE set, and there rubocop is 13/16 = 81% — far past the 0.50 W-CONFOUND threshold. Because STEP 2d is computed over all instances while every other step operates on eligible ones, the flag under-fires exactly where it matters. Ruby is the case that shows it. Concrete consequence: any Ruby finding drawn from the eligible pool is a rubocop finding unless a second repo is deliberately funded, which is why I made the primary representative fpm-1829 rather than the safer rubocop-13424.

3. LONG PROBLEM STATEMENTS ARE ANTI-CORRELATED WITH MEASURABILITY IN RUBY. fastlane holds the four longest Ruby statements (69351, 17477, 14743, 12011 chars) and loses all 7 instances to X-SMALL — its repo maximum scope is 13, below the class-I cut, so no fastlane instance can be sampled at any budget. fastlane-19207's 69351-char statement, 4.6x the next longest, buys a 10-test fence. Same pattern in fluentd (8179 chars -> scope 5; 6388 -> scope 1). Reading long statements to find big tasks would have been actively misleading here.

4. RUBY HAS NO NEGATIVE CONTROL. No eligible Ruby repo fires W-NOLEV (minimum spread among repos with an eligible instance is jekyll at 10x; rubocop 17.9x, fluentd 20x, fpm 15.7x). The one flat repo is faker at 1.78x, and both faker rows are X-SMALL. So the jq role — an instance that provably cannot move its repo's fence — has no Ruby analogue, and the 'instance effect vanishes' prediction cannot be tested in Ruby.

5. THREE OF THE NINETEEN CSV FEATURES ARE IDENTICALLY ZERO ACROSS ALL 44 RUBY ROWS: touches_header, touches_build, touches_core. touches_core is zero by definition (`int(lang in COMPILED)`), and touches_build fires on only 3/300 corpus-wide. So a fifth of the feature vector carries no within-Ruby information whatsoever.

6. ps_has_traceback IS PROVABLY BROKEN FOR RUBY, NOT JUST STRUCTURALLY SUSPECT. It reads 0 for all 44 rows, yet fluentd-3641's statement contains a 12-frame Ruby backtrace (`.../openssl/ssl.rb:239:in 'peeraddr'` and nine more). The extractor's regex only matches `Traceback|panic:|at Foo(x:1)|#N 0x`, so Ruby's `file.rb:LINE:in 'method'` format is invisible. known_limits #2 asserted this by construction for Ruby; this is the direct observation.

7. THE CLASS-I SCOPE THRESHOLD IS DOING MORE DAMAGE THAN THE SPEC'S CORPUS-WIDE FIGURE SUGGESTS, AND ITS WORST CASE IS ONE TEST WIDE. Ruby loses 28/44 = 64% to X-SMALL against the corpus-wide 35%. rubocop-13579 is excluded at scope 19 — one test below the cut — despite 4 F2P (tied for the most in rubocop) and ps_chars 3610. It is the first row to re-admit if the layer-2 probe raises rubocop's measured floor. Two of the three eligible non-rubocop rows (fluentd-3641, jekyll-8167) sit exactly ON the cut at 20, so the entire non-rubocop Ruby frame rests on a threshold derived from ten measured points.

8. A WITHIN-RUBOCOP CONTRAST IS PARTLY SELF-DEFEATING, WHICH MAKES IT WORTH RUNNING. representatives.rationale: Only one taxonomy category exists in Rust (all 7 Rust repos map to mech A), so this is the single required representative. Chosen on all three stated criteria. (1) Highest confidence available: zero warn flags - ps_chars=2068 with a repro so no W-READ, patch 1 file/1 hunk/1 add so no W-BIGDIFF, ruff is 7/43 = 16% of Rust so no W-CONFOUND, repo spread 26.8x so no W-NOLEV. (2) Largest fence prospect among non-tokio eligible rows: scope=1+133=134 is the biggest outside tokio, and it sits in a large multi-crate workspace where an edit inside a lint-rule crate forces a wide downstream rustc rebuild - so both the compile term and the runner term should be materially present, which is exactly what class A predicts and refuses to rank. (3) Repo diversity: the banked Rust reference is tokio-6551, so picking ruff adds a second Rust repo and makes Rust the only language in the corpus that can support a language-level claim (known_limits 6 needs >= 2 sampled repos). Bonus: because ruff's front-end is `cargo test` just as tokio's was, this episode is also the cleanest available test of the tagger inversion in known_limits 3 - if ruff again reports tests(rust)-dominant while its own argv log is rustc-dominant, the artefact is confirmed as systematic rather than tokio-specific.

SURPRISES, most important first.

1. RUST ADDS NO TAXONOMIC INFORMATION AT ALL. The mentor's <language x type> grid has exactly ONE Rust cell and it is already filled by tokio-6551. There is no search/edit/test/build split to find inside Rust, because the mechanism axis is a function of repo and every Rust repo is class A. Any further Rust episode must be justified by the within-repo scope tier, never as "a new Rust type".

2. RUST IS THE CORPUS'S BEST-SPREAD LANGUAGE, AND THAT IS THE REAL FINDING. Seven repos, largest share tokio 9/43 = 21%, so W-CONFOUND fires nowhere in Rust - unlike C++ (fmt 11/12) or JavaScript (preact 17/31), which known_limits 6 says can never be de-confounded. Rust therefore needs only ONE more episode in a second repo to clear the ">= 2 sampled repos per language" bar for a language-level claim. That is the cheapest available upgrade from an existence claim to a language claim anywhere in the study, and it argues for spending the Rust episode outside tokio.

3. THE HEADLINE WITHIN-TOKIO SPREAD OF 42x IS NOT MEASURABLE. The 42x comes from tokio-6603 (scope 85) over tokio-4384 (scope 2), but 4384 is X-SMALL and would be pre-rejected. The widest within-tokio pair that survives the gates is 6603 (85) vs 4898 (13), only ~6.5x, and against the already-banked 6551 (22) it is 3.9x. So the S-vs-L design in STEP 5 is sound for tokio but its usable dynamic range is ~4-6x, not 42x - worth restating before that number is quoted in support of "the instance dominates the language".

4. THE BANKED RUST REFERENCE IS A MID-LEVERAGE INSTANCE. tokio-6551 is tier M (rank 3 of 6 tokio eligible), and four tokio instances have >= its scope. The Rust row in the reference table is therefore not a "large" tokio task, which matters when it is compared against php-cs-fixer (scope 237) or gson (scope 6).

5. THE ONE RUST X-DEGEN IS A GENUINE RULE-VS-MAGNITUDE CONFLICT. coreutils-6377 has ps_chars=135, just 15 under the cut, yet scope=62 with 4 F2P tests in a large workspace - it would almost certainly have cleared the 20 core-s / 1000 Ginstr gate. Reading it confirms the exclusion is right for the right reason (a bare man-page quote asking for a feature, no repro, no named symbol - the carbon-2813 shape), but it makes explicit that R1 rejects on AGENT-degeneracy risk while R2/R3 reject on fence size. Those are two different failure modes sharing one gate, and 6377 is the clearest case in the corpus where they disagree.

6. FOUR RUST ROWS SIT EXACTLY ON OR WITHIN TWO TESTS OF THE MECH-A CUT: axum-1119 and coreutils-6731 are accepted at scope=10 exactly; tokio-6838 and coreutils-6690 are rejected at 8; ruff-15394 is rejected at 9 despite test_add=226. Five of 43 Rust instances (12%) are decided by a threshold that was calibrated on a single measured point (gin at scope 2 versus prometheus at 12). This is the weakest quantitative part of the frame for Rust, and it is exactly what the layer-2 repo probe is for.

7. bat AND axum ARE STRUCTURALLY WEAK AND SHOULD NOT BE SAMPLED. They carry the most exclusions (bat 5/8, axum 4/7) and their entire eligible ranges are 13-29 and 10-21 - their L tiers are below tokio's M. Meanwhile W-BIGDIFF fires on 3 of axum's 3 eligible rows (patches up to 7 files / 133 added lines), a reminder that axum's large diffs are a harness-fence covariate with no tool-fence meaning.

8. TIER IS DEGENERATE WHENEVER A REPO HAS ONE ELIGIBLE INSTANCE. ripgrep-2576 is simultaneously its repo's min and max; STEP 3 has no rule for n_eligible=1 (tier F is reserved for W-NOLEV, and ripgrep's spread is 86x). I assigned L and flagged it. Worth patching the spec: define tier for n_eligible=1 explicitly rather than leaving it to the reader.

9. A TESTABLE PREDICTION FOR WHOEVER RUNS THE REPRESENTATIVE. Class A predicts a mixture but the two banked A rows disagree in opposite directions (prometheus reports compile 62%, tokio reports tests 87%). Within Rust the compile intercept should scale with workspace size: ruff, nushell and coreutils are large multi-crate workspaces, tokio and axum are comparatively self-contained, bat and ripgrep are small. If ruff-15356 comes back tests(rust)-dominant while its own argv log is rustc-dominant, that confirms the TAG_PRIORITY artefact in known_limits 3 as systematic rather than a tokio quirk - and no B-vs-A boundary should be drawn until it is fixed.

SURPRISES, most important first.

1. THE SPEC'S OWN SCOPE GATE IS NOT SELF-CONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN FENCE FLOOR. Fitting the three measured PHP points (carbon-2813 scope 4 -> 6.6 core-s, laravel-51890 scope 8 -> 6.4, php-cs-fixer-7523 scope 237 -> 105.3) gives fence ~= 2.94 + 0.432*scope. Setting that to the layer-3 floor of 20 core-s requires scope >= ~40, NOT 20. Consequence: 8 of the 18 selectable PHP instances pass R2 but are PREDICTED TO FAIL the post-episode gate -- the entire I.S tier for carbon and laravel (2981, 3073, 3005, 48573, 52680, 53949) plus the M-tier boundary rows carbon-3098 and laravel-53696. Read literally, PHP's small-instance cell is unfillable: the only S candidate above the floor is php-cs-fixer-7998, which is in the already-sampled repo. Either raise 1b to scope >= 40 for PHP, or accept that "one task per <language, type>" has no S entry for PHP and publish that cell as structurally empty.

2. THE 0.43 core-s/TEST SLOPE HAS THE WRONG CAUSAL STORY, AND I HAVE DIRECT EVIDENCE. I read the banked argv log of the profiled php-cs-fixer episode (/home/thu/InferSuite/local_agents/ML_multiling/data/glm_replay_swe_php-cs-fixer). The agent did NOT run the graded test set. It ran DIRECTORY-level and whole-suite PHPUnit: `php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Fixer/` (648 argv samples), `tests/Fixer/FunctionNotation/ tests/Fixer/Whitespace/` (826), `tests/Fixer/Operator/` (762), and bare `php vendor/bin/phpunit` with no path at all (110 samples across three whitespace variants) -- the ENTIRE suite. So the 105.3 core-s reflects the agent's choice of command breadth, not n_f2p+n_p2p. The slope is a coincidental 3-point fit across 2 repos. Correct reading, which I have used throughout: n_f2p is 1 for 33 of 43 PHP rows, so scope is ~entirely n_p2p = the case count of the test CLASS the test_patch touches, i.e. a LOWER BOUND on executed test volume (the cost of the narrowest sensible run). It bounds the floor and says nothing about the ceiling. That keeps the gate's DIRECTION valid (small scope => even the narrowest run is tiny) while invalidating upward magnitude extrapolation in both directions. This is the strongest argument yet for the layer-2 repo probe: the quantity that actually needs measuring is per-repo full-suite cost (ceiling) and single-file cost (floor), both repo attributes.

3. FOUR OF THE FIVE BINARY "STATIC PREDICTORS" ARE EXACTLY CONSTANT INSIDE PHP -- independent confirmation of the deleted S and D categories. ps_has_traceback = 0 for 43/43 (structural: the regex has no PHP pattern, exactly as known_limits #2 says). ps_has_repro = 1 for 42/43 (only the degenerate carbon-2813 is 0). touches_header = 0/43. touches_core = 0/43 (it is a compiled-language dummy). touches_build fires on exactly ONE PHP row and it is carbon-2813, the degenerate reject -- reproducing the spec's recall 0/1, precision 0/1 verdict on the record. Within PHP these five features carry ZERO information; the only live features are scope, ps_chars and repo.

4. PATCH SIZE IS ANTI-CORRELATED WITH SCOPE IN PHP. Spearman(scope, patch_add) = -0.13 over all 43. The four largest-scope instances (7523 s237, 48636 s168, 2752 s151, 52684 s151) have patch_add of 2, 1, 2, 9 and patch_files = 1 in every case, while the minimum-scope row (3659, scope 2) has patch_files 4 / patch_hunks 10 / patch_add 61. The best PHP fence candidates are one-line fixes sitting behind large test classes. W-BIGDIFF must stay a harness-fence covariate; in PHP, reading it as a CPU signal would invert the ranking.

5. phpspreadsheet IS STRUCTURALLY A NEGATIVE CONTROL, NOT A TIER REPO. 8 of its 10 instances are X-SMALL -- the harshest attrition of any repo I saw. The 2 survivors span 42-59, a 1.40x spread, so W-NOLEV fires and STEP 3 forces tier F. It cannot host a within-repo S-vs-L pair at any budget. NOTE AN AMBIGUITY IN THE SPEC: flag 2c says "over the repo" without naming the population, while 2b says "over the eligible instances". Over ALL 10 instances phpspreadsheet's spread is 29.5x and W-NOLEV would NOT fire. I used the ELIGIBLE population, for consistency with 2b and because the flag's stated purpose ("the instance cannot move the fence in this repo") is about the frame you can actually sample. Worth pinning down in the spec, since it changes phpspreadsheet's label from L/M to F. Either way the tier split is degenerate (a tercile over n=2), so F is the honest label.

6. PHP IS THE BEST LANGUAGE IN THE CORPUS FOR A LANGUAGE-LEVEL CLAIM. W-CONFOUND fires on no PHP repo: the largest share is laravel at 13/43 = 0.30, and all four repos sit at 0.23-0.30. With 4 repos and >=2 sampled, "PHP is interpreted-suite dominated" is a defensible language-level statement -- and the four representatives above put one episode in each repo, so two of them already discharge the ">= 2 sampled repos" requirement.

I applied X-DUP only to php-cs-fixer, the one PHP repo with an ACCEPTED banked episode. carbon and laravel each burned an episode (2813, 51890) but both were PARKED and produced no banked cell -- and under the current rules neither would ever have been run (both are pre-rejected statically). The spec's own high-leverage spreads are computed over ALL instances, but an S-vs-L pair needs BOTH members eligible — so the achievable leverage is far smaller than advertised. babel: 43.7x over all 5 instances (the spec's 'babel 44x') but only 9.4x over its 4 eligible (56 -> 524). preact: 38.0x over all 17 (the spec's 'preact 38x') but only 3.6x over its 8 eligible (21 -> 76). Recommend the spec quote eligible-only spreads wherever leverage is claimed.

3. The babel S-vs-L pair is available for one episode, with the S half already paid. babel-15445 (banked, accepted) labels as N.S at scope 56; babel-14532 sits at scope 524 and labels N.L. One more episode completes a within-repo pair with repo, language and toolchain held fixed — the only design known_limits #7 accepts as evidence for the headline 'the instance dominates fence size far more than the language' claim, which is currently carried by fmt-vs-gin (a pair that differs in language, repo, toolchain AND instance at once). This is arguably the highest-value JavaScript episode available, and it is a different objective from category representation, so I did not let it displace the representative; it is the runner_up and should be pre-declared under STEP 1g to avoid X-DUP.

All three N.S/marginal rows (preact-3567 scope 21, preact-4436 scope 26, preact-3562 scope 32) fall where the measured PHP zero-intercept slope (0.43 core-s per test on a ~5 core-s intercept) predicts 14, 16 and 19 core-s — all UNDER the 20 core-s floor. The R2 threshold of 20 tests and the layer-3 floor of 20 core-s are mutually inconsistent under the only slope the study has measured; slope-consistency would require scope >= 35. Either the gate will keep firing on legitimately-labelled S instances, or R2 should be raised for mech N once layer-2 probe data exists. Practical consequence: JavaScript can populate N.L and N.M reliably but cannot be expected to populate N.S without paying for parked episodes.

So the W-BIGDIFF harness-fence covariate is structurally unobtainable in JavaScript: eligibility and diff size are anti-correlated here, because large JS diffs land in axios and three.js while large test scopes land in babel and preact.

The longest statement in the language (preact-3739, 8774 chars) is X-SMALL at scope 13 with the minimum possible gold patch (1 file / 1 hunk / 1 add); the second longest (axios-6539, 3824 chars) has the smallest scope in the language (1, with n_p2p = 0).
